title: Do Cuttlefish Dream of Electric Shrimp? A Natural History Note on Behavioral Quiescence Strategies in Wild European Cuttlefish (Sepia officinalis)
content:
Continuous video stills documenting an unprovoked alert-to-quiescent-to-alert transition sequence in an individual wild Sepia officinalis. Panels (A–B) show the individual exhibiting localized arm L1/R1 twitching and low-amplitude ground tracking while slowly drifting down towards substrate in an apparently uncontrolled manner, utilizing a low-contrast mottled/weak zebra composite pattern. Panels (C–D) document a rapid arousal sequence: the individual abandons the falling motion, drifts vertically, and rapidly accentuates its chromatic contrast to a bold blanche signal to a zebra/mottled layout upon visual alignment with the recording diver. The sequence appears to show the cuttlefish “waking up” from a deeper relaxed state.


ABSTRACT

Laboratory-based ethological studies have identified highly structured sleep-like and quiescent states in coleoid cephalopods. However, identifying these physiological states in wild populations remains challenging due to observer-induced flight behaviors. Presented here are a secondary micro-kinetic analysis of an unprovoked wild cohort of six sub-adult European cuttlefish (Sepia officinalis) recorded continuously for 55 min in their natural habitat. Quantitative point-process analysis of localized motor events revealed that micro-somatic adjustments (low-amplitude arm L1/R1 twitches, N = 64) are significantly clustered, exhibiting a median inter-event interval of 2.08 s. First-order Markov chain modeling demonstrates a highly structured behavioral transition network centered on a composite chromatic state (Mottled + Zebra Pattern composite), with a restricted probability (14.3%) of transitioning into absolute motor arrest (Mantle fin stop). While limited by sample size and a lack of physiological or electrophysiological metrics, these field observations provide a rare, non-invasive behavioral baseline that mirrors the micro-kinetic patterns reported in controlled laboratory sleep settings. We also provide verbal descriptions of quiescent states observed.
author: Gavan M. Cooke
